st: The 1908 plat book of Racine and Kenosha counties draws a schoolhouse here (on the lake shore, sec. 32/29). It is built-up ground today.
t: Schoolyards were used for 30 to 60 years. Look for the cleared square, a well or pump and lilacs; on a 1938 aerial the yard often shows as a bare patch by the road.

n: Church site, sec. 32 T3N R23E (1908 plat)
v: Coins, religious medals, rings, buttons from churchgoers and socials
st: The 1908 plat book of Racine and Kenosha counties draws a church here (on the Somers line, sec. 32). It is open field today with a building nearby.
t: The yard and the road edge in front of the door are best; churches held picnics and socials outside. Leave any burials alone.
